root_cause.text: The Amlogic SPI flash controller driver (`aml_sfc_probe()` in `spi-amlogic-spifc-a4.c`) registered a NAND on-host ECC engine without any matching cleanup path, so probe failures and device removal left the ECC engine registered and leaked stale state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `aml_sfc_unregister_ecc_engine()` calling `nand_ecc_unregister_on_host_hw_engine(eng)` and hooks it with `devm_add_action_or_reset()` immediately after successful registration, and the commit message explicitly says teardown was “missing from both probe unwind and remove-time cleanup.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a cleanup helper to unregister the ECC engine during driver teardown.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function `aml_sfc_unregister_ecc_engine(void *data)` was added. It casts the `data` pointer to `struct nand_ecc_engine *` and calls `nand_ecc_unregister_on_host_hw_engine(eng)`.
intent_record.how: This adds a dedicated cleanup callback that can unregister the NAND ECC engine when invoked, likely allowing the driver to tie ECC engine teardown to a managed resource or exit path and ensure proper deregistration at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add managed cleanup for the ECC engine registration to ensure it is unregistered on probe failure or device removal.
intent_record.what: The probe function now calls devm_add_action_or_reset() after successfully registering the Aml host ECC engine, passing aml_sfc_unregister_ecc_engine and &sfc->ecc_eng, and returns a dev_err_probe() failure if adding that managed action fails.
intent_record.how: This makes ECC engine unregistration part of the device-managed cleanup path, so if probe later fails or the device is removed, the ECC engine will be automatically unregistered, preventing resource leaks or stale registrations.
